items.exemplar:
A. The diagram shows a three-legged circuit: New England ships carried rum to Africa, traded it for enslaved people, and returned with sugar and molasses from the West Indies. The pattern reveals how deeply the northern colonial economy depended on slavery even where plantations were rare.

B. One way the imperial system affected the colonies was through the Navigation Acts of 1660 and 1663, which forced colonists to ship tobacco, rice, and sugar to England and to route European goods through English ports, enriching English merchants at colonial expense.

C. Colonists resisted tighter control by smuggling and by defying royal authority — Massachusetts's defiance of the Navigation Acts helped provoke the Dominion of New England, and colonial assemblies used their 'power of the purse' to frustrate royal governors.
parts: A. Identify and briefly explain ONE pattern shown in the triangular trade diagram.
B. Briefly explain ONE way the British imperial system affected the colonies.
C. Briefly explain ONE way the colonies resisted greater British control.
items.stimulus: The diagram shows the triangular trade of the 1700s. One arrow runs from New England to West Africa labeled 'rum and manufactured goods.' A second arrow runs from West Africa to the West Indies labeled 'enslaved Africans (Middle Passage).' A third arrow runs from the West Indies back to New England labeled 'sugar and molasses.'
